   129	            id: "clip.timing", title: "Timing",
   130	            summary: { total() },
   131	            defaultExpanded: false,
   132	            rows: reverseRows(
   133	                over: clips,
   134	                mixed: { binding.mixed(clips()) { $0.source.isReversed } }))
   135	    }
   136	
   137	    /// The Reverse group — the box, the state readout and the retry button —
   138	    /// over whatever clips the section speaks for: the one clip of a
   139	    /// single-clip Timing, every media clip of a multi-clip one. One op per
   140	    /// clip, all in one `apply`, so the fan-out is a single undo step.
   141	    ///
   142	    /// **Reverse carries a state readout that no other control here needs.**
   143	    /// AVFoundation cannot play a clip backwards, so ticking the box does not
   144	    /// change the picture by itself: it makes the app pre-render the frames
   145	    /// (spec §11), and until they exist the clip draws a slate rather than
   146	    /// lying about which way it is going. The readout says which of those the
   147	    /// clip is in, and the button is what restarts a render the user stopped —
   148	    /// the one path back from `ReverseStatus.stopped`, since nothing retries
   149	    /// on its own.
   150	    func reverseRows(
   151	        over clips: @escaping () -> [ClipSnapshot], mixed: (() -> Bool)?
   152	    ) -> [NSView] {
   153	        let binding = self.binding
   154	        /// One line for what may be several clips. Stopped outranks pending
   155	        /// deliberately: it is the state with something to do about it, and a
   156	        /// "Rendering…" that hid a stopped clip behind a rendering one would
   157	        /// grey out the only button that could fix it.
   158	        func status() -> ReverseStatus {
   159	            guard let document = binding.document else { return .off }
   160	            let states = clips().map { document.reverseStatus(of: $0) }
   161	            for state in [ReverseStatus.stopped, .pending, .unavailable, .ready]
   162	            where states.contains(state) {
   163	                return state
   164	            }
   165	            return .off
   166	        }
   167	        let render = OptionButtonControl(
   168	            title: "Render Reverse",
   169	            action: {
   170	                guard let document = binding.document else { return }
   171	                guard let next = clips().first(where: {
   172	                    document.reverseStatus(of: $0) == .stopped
   173	                })
   174	                else { return }
   175	                // **Pitfall:** one press starts ONE media.
   176	                // `ensureReversedMedia` refuses to open a second sheet while
   177	                // one is up, so un-refusing every stopped clip here would
   178	                // leave all but the first reading "Rendering…" with nothing
   179	                // rendering. Retried one at a time, the readout keeps saying
   180	                // "Not rendered" while any remain, and the next press takes
   181	                // the next one.
   182	                document.retryReversedMedia(for: next)
   183	            },
   184	            enabled: { status() == .stopped },
   185	            onEdit: {})
   186	        render.toolTip = "Render the reversed frames these clips need"
   187	        return [
   188	            inspectorCheckRow(
   189	                "Reverse", binding, name: "Reverse",
   190	                read: { clips().first?.source.isReversed ?? false },
   191	                ops: { value in
   192	                    clips().map { ReelOp.setReversed(clip: $0.id, reversed: value) }
   193	                },
   194	                mixed: mixed, resets: false),
   195	            inspectorRow("Reversed frames", [inspectorReadout { status().summary }]),
   196	            inspectorButtonRow([render]),
   197	        ]
   198	    }
   199	}

     2	
     3	/// Clip ▸ Split at Shot Changes (spec §11 CJ-28, CJ-29; road map
     4	/// "creator-jobs" CJ2b) — the menu half of `split_at_shots`. The planner is
     5	/// `ShotSplit`, which the tool calls too; this file is the door: the
     6	/// selection's targets, the Analyzing sheet when the shots analysis misses
     7	/// the cache, and the edit.
     8	///
     9	/// With every window cached the split lands at once, in the menu's event
    10	/// (`applyEdit`). Otherwise the sheet makes what is missing; its hand-back
    11	/// is not an AppKit event, so the split goes through `performGroupedEdit`
    12	/// (app/CLAUDE.md's undo pitfall, `finishSynchronizeAudio`'s shape), and
    13	/// only onto the project handle and scope the press read. Nothing to split,
    14	/// no window or a sheet already up beep; a refusal beeps and puts its
    15	/// sentence at the inspector's foot (spec §11 CI-10).
    16	extension EditorViewController {
    17	
    18	    @objc func splitAtShotChanges(_ sender: Any?) {
    19	        guard let document, let window = view.window, window.attachedSheet == nil else {
    20	            NSSound.beep()
    21	            return
    22	        }
    23	        let targets = ShotSplit.targets(selectedClips.map(\.id), in: document.editedProject)
    24	            .targets
    25	        guard !targets.isEmpty else {
    26	            NSSound.beep()
    27	            return
    28	        }
    29	        let wants: [ShotSplit.Want]
    30	        do {
    31	            wants = try ShotSplit.wants(targets, in: document)
    32	        } catch {
    33	            refuseShotSplit(error.localizedDescription, document: document)
    34	            return
    35	        }
    36	        guard !wants.isEmpty else {
    37	            commitShotSplit(targets, document: document, grouped: false)
    38	            return
    39	        }
    40	        let asked = document.project
    41	        let scope = document.scope
    42	        let rows = wants.map { AnalyzingSheetController.Row(name: $0.media.name, request: $0.request) }
    43	        presentAsSheet(
    44	            AnalyzingSheetController(
    45	                document: document, command: ShotSplit.actionName, rows: rows
    46	            ) { [weak self, weak document] outcome in
    47	                guard let self, let document else { return }
    48	                self.finishShotSplit(
    49	                    outcome, targets: targets, asked: asked, scope: scope, document: document)
    50	            })
    51	    }
    52	
    53	    /// The Analyzing sheet's answer: refused when the document's project or
    54	    /// scope is no longer the one the press read; a failed analysis named;
    55	    /// else the plan, as one grouped step.
    56	    private func finishShotSplit(
    57	        _ outcome: AnalyzingSheetController.Outcome, targets: [ShotSplit.Target],
    58	        asked: ReelProject, scope: UInt32?, document: ProjectDocument
    59	    ) {
    60	        guard document.project === asked, document.scope == scope else {
    61	            refuseShotSplit(
    62	                "the project changed while \(ShotSplit.actionName) was analyzing, so nothing "
    63	                    + "was split. Choose \(ShotSplit.actionName) again.", document: document)
    64	            return
    65	        }
    66	        switch outcome {
    67	        case .failed(let name, let why):
    68	            refuseShotSplit("The shots analysis of “\(name)” failed: \(why).", document: document)
    69	        case .landed:
    70	            commitShotSplit(targets, document: document, grouped: true)
    71	        }
    72	    }
    73	
    74	    /// Plans from the store and applies: in the menu's event when `grouped`
    75	    /// is false, else as one explicit undo group. No cut beeps.
    76	    private func commitShotSplit(
    77	        _ targets: [ShotSplit.Target], document: ProjectDocument, grouped: Bool
    78	    ) {
    79	        let plan: ShotSplit.Plan
    80	        do {
    81	            plan = try ShotSplit.plan(targets, in: document)
    82	        } catch {
    83	            refuseShotSplit(error.localizedDescription, document: document)
    84	            return
    85	        }
    86	        guard !plan.ops.isEmpty else {
    87	            NSSound.beep()
    88	            return
    89	        }
    90	        if grouped {
    91	            document.performGroupedEdit(ShotSplit.actionName, plan.ops)
    92	        } else {
    93	            document.applyEdit(ShotSplit.actionName, plan.ops)
    94	        }
    95	    }
    96	
    97	    /// A beep and the sentence at the inspector's foot.
    98	    private func refuseShotSplit(_ reason: String, document: ProjectDocument) {
    99	        NSSound.beep()
   100	        NotificationCenter.default.post(
   101	            name: .projectDocumentDidRefuse, object: document,

     3	/// The `shots` kind (spec §11 CJ-24; road map "creator-jobs" CJ2a): hard
     4	/// cuts from a deterministic picture difference, no ML.
     5	///
     6	/// **The signature** is spike CJ-S4's: a 4 × 4 × 4 colour histogram — the
     7	/// top two bits of each of R, G and B — of the frame at long side 256, in
     8	/// whole-pixel counts. **The distance** is their L1 summed exactly in
     9	/// integers and divided once by the pixel count (0…2), so two distances
    10	/// equal in counts are equal to the bit — a flash's two sides tie, as the
    11	/// cut rule's tie-break needs.
    12	///
    13	/// **Stored per grid index** (`frames.bin`, one 16-byte little-endian record
    14	/// per index from 0: `Int64` pts in ticks, −1 for no frame, `Float32` d1,
    15	/// `Float32` d2): d1(i) is the distance to p1(i), the greatest index below i
    16	/// holding a frame; d2(i) to p2(i), the greatest below p1(i); none → 0. Both
    17	/// depend only on the frame and the two kept frames before it (CJ-22).
    18	///
    19	/// **The cut rule, applied when answered** (`cuts`): frame i is a cut when
    20	/// d1(i) ≥ T; d2(n(i)) ≥ T, n(i) the least index above i holding a frame,
    21	/// the test passing when no frame lies in i+1…i+m+1 or at the media's end;
    22	/// and d1(i) is the largest d1 over i−m…i+m, an empty index counting 0, ties
    23	/// to the earlier. T = 0.34, m = 12; the read margin is m + 1.
    24	enum AnalysisShots {
    25	    static let longSide = 256
    26	    static let threshold: Float = 0.34
    27	    static let neighbourhood = 12
    28	    /// The read margin, m + 1 indices each side.
    29	    static var margin: Int { neighbourhood + 1 }
    30	    static let payloadName = "frames.bin"
    31	    static let recordSize = 16
    32	    /// A job publishes at each range's end and after this much wall time.
    33	    static let publishInterval: TimeInterval = 30
    34	
    35	    /// What the stored values depend on (never T or m): the stamp's digest.
    36	    static let parameters: [String: Any] = [
    37	        "signature": "rgb_histogram", "bits_per_channel": 2, "long_side": longSide,
    38	        "distance": "l1_counts",
    39	    ]
    40	
    41	    struct Record: Equatable {
    42	        var pts: Int64
    43	        var d1: Float
    44	        var d2: Float
    45	
    46	        static let empty = Record(pts: -1, d1: 0, d2: 0)
    47	        var holdsFrame: Bool { pts >= 0 }
    48	    }
    49	
    50	    // MARK: - The signature
    51	
    52	    /// 64 counts of a picture's colours by their top two bits.
    53	    static func signature(_ picture: AnalysisPicture) -> [Int32] {
    54	        var counts = [Int32](repeating: 0, count: 64)
    55	        for y in 0..<picture.height {
    56	            let row = picture.bytes + y * picture.bytesPerRow
    57	            for x in 0..<picture.width {
    58	                let p = row + x * 4
    59	                let bin = Int(p[2] >> 6) << 4 | Int(p[1] >> 6) << 2 | Int(p[0] >> 6)
    60	                counts[bin] += 1
    61	            }
    62	        }
    63	        return counts
    64	    }
    65	
    66	    /// L1 of two signatures over the first one's pixel count.
    67	    static func distance(_ a: [Int32], _ b: [Int32]) -> Float {
    68	        var sum: Int64 = 0
    69	        var total: Int64 = 0

    71	            sum += Int64(abs(a[i] - b[i]))
    72	            total += Int64(a[i])
    73	        }

   108	    static func merge(

   110	    ) {

   113	            var tail = Data()
   114	            for _ in 0..<((length - data.count) / recordSize) { tail.append(contentsOf: bytes(of: .empty)) }

   127	    // MARK: - The cut rule
   128	
   129	    /// The cuts among `window`'s indices of `records` (the whole grid).
   130	    static func cuts(
   131	        _ records: [Record], in window: ClosedRange<Int>, threshold: Float = threshold,
   132	        m: Int = neighbourhood
   133	    ) -> [Int] {
   134	        let n = records.count
   135	        func holds(_ i: Int) -> Bool { i >= 0 && i < n && records[i].holdsFrame }
   136	        let low = max(0, window.lowerBound)
   137	        let high = min(n - 1, window.upperBound)
   138	        guard low <= high else { return [] }
   139	        var found: [Int] = []
   140	        for i in low...high where holds(i) && records[i].d1 >= threshold {
   141	            let d = records[i].d1
   142	            // A single flash returning to the shot: the next frame within
   143	            // m + 1 must differ from the frame before this one too.
   144	            var next: Int?
   145	            if i + 1 <= min(n - 1, i + m + 1) {
   146	                next = (i + 1...min(n - 1, i + m + 1)).first(where: holds)
   147	            }
   148	            if let next, records[next].d2 < threshold { continue }
   149	            var largest = true
   150	            for j in max(0, i - m)...min(n - 1, i + m) where j != i {
   151	                let other = holds(j) ? records[j].d1 : 0
   152	                if (j < i && other >= d) || (j > i && other > d) {
   153	                    largest = false
   154	                    break
   155	                }
   156	            }
   157	            if largest { found.append(i) }
   158	        }
   159	        return found
   160	    }

   162	    // MARK: - The job
   163	
   164	    /// Runs `request`'s ranges in order, publishing at each range's end and
   165	    /// every `publishInterval`. False when `cancelled()` stopped it.
   166	    /// `progress` hears done / total of the ranges' indices after each
   167	    /// stored frame (the Analyzing sheet's bar, spec §11 CJ-28).
   168	    static func run(
   169	        _ request: AnalysisRequest, cancelled: () -> Bool,
   170	        progress: (Double) -> Void = { _ in }
   171	    ) throws -> Bool {
   172	        let grid = AnalysisGrid(media: request.media)
   173	        let source = AnalysisFrames.Source(
   174	            media: request.media, url: request.url, input: request.input)
   175	        let total = max(1, request.ranges.reduce(0) { $0 + $1.count })
   176	        var before = 0
   177	        for range in request.ranges {
   178	            var records: [Int: Record] = [:]
   179	            var p1: [Int32]?
   180	            var p2: [Int32]?
   181	            var coveredFrom = range.lowerBound
   182	            var lastIndex = range.lowerBound - 1
   183	            var lastPublish = Date()
   184	            let finished = try AnalysisFrames.read(
   185	                range: range, grid: grid, source: source, longSide: longSide,
   186	                cancelled: cancelled
   187	            ) { k, pts, picture in
   188	                let signature = signature(picture)
   189	                if k >= range.lowerBound {
   190	                    records[k] = Record(
   191	                        pts: pts, d1: p1.map { distance(signature, $0) } ?? 0,
   192	                        d2: p2.map { distance(signature, $0) } ?? 0)
   193	                    lastIndex = k
   194	                    progress(Double(before + k - range.lowerBound + 1) / Double(total))
   195	                }
   196	                p2 = p1
   197	                p1 = signature
   198	                if Date().timeIntervalSince(lastPublish) >= publishInterval,
   199	                    lastIndex >= coveredFrom
   200	                {
   201	                    try publish(request, grid: grid, covered: coveredFrom...lastIndex, records)
   202	                    records.removeAll()
   203	                    coveredFrom = lastIndex + 1
   204	                    lastPublish = Date()
   205	                }
   206	            }
   207	            guard finished else { return false }
   208	            if coveredFrom <= range.upperBound {
   209	                try publish(request, grid: grid, covered: coveredFrom...range.upperBound, records)
   210	            }
   211	            before += range.count
   212	        }
   213	        return true
   214	    }

   216	    private static func publish(
   217	        _ request: AnalysisRequest, grid: AnalysisGrid, covered: ClosedRange<Int>,
   218	        _ records: [Int: Record]
   219	    ) throws {
   220	        try AnalysisStore.publish(
   221	            kind: .shots, cacheDir: request.cacheDir, mediaID: request.media.id,
   222	            stamp: request.stamp, covered: [covered], files: [payloadName]
   223	        ) { data in
   224	            merge(&data, count: grid.count, records: records, covered: [covered])
   225	        }
   226	    }

     4	/// FORWARD media to clip ticks, through its source map when it ramps, its
     5	/// speed when not, and the reversed mirror first when it plays backwards.
     6	struct AnalysisClipTimes {
     7	    let id: UInt32
     8	    let start: Ticks
     9	    let sourceIn: Ticks
    10	    let speed: Double
    11	    let pivot: Ticks?
    12	    let map: SourceMap?
    13	    /// The played window in the forward media's ticks, [lower, upper).
    14	    let window: ClosedRange<Ticks>
    15	
    16	    init(clip: ClipSnapshot, media: MediaSnapshot, map: SourceMap?) {
    17	        id = clip.id
    18	        start = clip.start
    19	        speed = clip.speed > 0 && clip.speed.isFinite ? clip.speed : 1
    20	        let ramp = map.flatMap { $0.ramped ? $0 : nil }
    21	        self.map = ramp
    22	        sourceIn = ramp?.sourceIn ?? clip.source.sourceIn
    23	        let length = ramp?.sourceLength ?? Transcriber.contentLength(of: clip)
    24	        pivot = clip.source.isReversed ? media.duration : nil
    25	        let played = sourceIn...(sourceIn + length)
    26	        let forward = pivot.map { ReverseMirror.mirrored(played, about: $0) } ?? played
    27	        let low = min(max(0, forward.lowerBound), media.duration)
    28	        window = low...max(low, min(media.duration, forward.upperBound))
    29	    }

    31	    /// Ticks from the clip's start, in its playing direction, at forward
    32	    /// source tick `source`.
    33	    func clipTime(ofSource source: Int64) -> Ticks {
    34	        let played = pivot.map { ReverseMirror.mirrored(source, about: $0) } ?? source
    35	        if let map { return Ticks(map.clip(atSource: Double(played)).rounded()) }
    36	        return Ticks((Double(played - sourceIn) / speed).rounded())
    37	    }

Moves a hard CUT — ⌥⇧-dragging a clip's edge. This clip's start and its predecessor's end both become `to`: one clip grows by exactly what the other loses, and the pair's outer edges and total length do not move. The predecessor is the clip on the same track ending EXACTLY at this one's start; with a gap or an overlap there instead, it is refused (an overlap is a transition — use set_transition_duration). Clamped so each clip keeps a frame and neither asks for source it does not have. The linked half of a detach_audio pair rolls its own cut too when it starts at the same time.

Frame Job finds the cuts on this Mac, with nothing sent anywhere and no key needed, and keeps them in the project's cache, so a second split of the same footage starts at once. While they are being found the **Analyzing** sheet shows each file with a bar: "Waiting" until its first frame is read, then the share done, then "Done". **Stop** closes the sheet and changes nothing; what was already found stays in the cache. If you change the project while the sheet is up, nothing is split and the inspector says to choose the command again.
